Shape Constraints for a Smooth

Source: R/shape.R
shape_constructors.Rd

Construct the shapes that scs() imposes on a smooth. shape_increasing() and shape_decreasing() give a monotone curve, with a slope of at least min_slope in absolute value; shape_convex() and shape_concave() give a curve of constant sign of curvature; the four combinations shape_increasing_convex(), shape_increasing_concave(), shape_decreasing_convex() and shape_decreasing_concave() give a monotone curve of constant sign of curvature.

Usage

shape_increasing(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  min_slope = 0,
  value = NULL
)

shape_decreasing(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  min_slope = 0,
  value = NULL
)

shape_convex(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  slope = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_concave(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  slope = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_increasing_convex(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_increasing_concave(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_decreasing_convex(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

shape_decreasing_concave(
  link = linkfunctions7::log_link(),
  value = NULL,
  left_slope_by = c("level", "shared")
)

Arguments

link

A linkfunctions7 link onto \((0, \infty)\), by default linkfunctions7::log_link(). linkfunctions7::softplus_link() is the other shipped choice.

min_slope

A single nonnegative number, the smallest slope in absolute value, or a vector of such numbers named by the levels of a factor by.

value

NULL, two finite numbers c(at = a, value = v), or a list list(at = a, value = v) whose elements are one number or a vector named by level: the smooth is \(v\) at \(a\). Unnamed, the first number is the point.

slope

NULL, or the same forms as value: the derivative of the smooth is \(v\) at \(a\).

left_slope_by

Under a factor by, whether the left slope of a curvature shape is a coefficient of each level ("level", the default) or one coefficient for every level ("shared"). "shared" without a factor by is an error.

Value

An S7 object of class ShapeMonotone (shape_increasing(), shape_decreasing()) or ShapeCurvature (the other six), both inheriting from shape_constraint.

Details

A monotone shape parametrizes the slopes of the B-spline coefficients on the Greville abscissae, \(s_j = \pm(\delta + g^{-1}(\gamma_j))\) with \(\delta\) = min_slope. A curvature shape keeps the slope at the left end free and parametrizes the second divided differences, \(\pm g^{-1}(\gamma_j)\). A combination constrains the slope as well, at the end where the slope is smallest in absolute value: the left end for an increasing convex or a decreasing concave curve, the right end for an increasing concave or a decreasing convex one, so that every slope keeps its sign. See shape_constraint for the map.

A value or a slope at a point

With value = c(at = a, value = v) the smooth satisfies \(f(a) = v\) exactly, and this constraint replaces the centering of scs(). With slope = c(at = a, value = v), which only shape_convex() and shape_concave() accept, it satisfies \(f'(a) = v\) exactly: the slope at the left end, the one free slope of these two shapes, is then written in terms of the second divided differences. The other shapes constrain every slope, so a slope at a point cannot be imposed on them by this elimination. The point \(a\) must lie in the interval of the basis, which the lower and upper arguments of the smoother can widen.

A value other than zero changes the fit only when no other term of the equation absorbs a constant (an intercept, the effects of a factor, an uncentered term), as in a formula that starts with 0 +. Otherwise the fit is the same for every \(v\), and \(v\) only moves the level between the intercept and the smooth; with \(v = 0\) the intercept is the linear predictor at \(a\).

Under a factor by

With a factor by in scs(), min_slope may be a vector named by the levels, and the point and the value of value or slope may be given by level in the list form, list(at = 0, value = c(a = 0, b = 1)). A curvature shape has one left slope per level by default; with left_slope_by = "shared" that slope (the free one of shape_convex() and shape_concave(), the anchored one of a combination) is one coefficient for every level. The anchored slope of a combination is penalized, so tying it is not available with by_hyper = "level" in scs(), which would penalize it once per level; a slope at a point removes the left slope and cannot be combined with a tie.

See also

scs(), shape_constraint.

Examples

shape_increasing()
#> <shape: increasing, link = log>
shape_decreasing(min_slope = 0.1)
#> <shape: decreasing, link = log, min_slope = 0.1>
shape_convex(link = linkfunctions7::softplus_link())
#> <shape: convex, link = softplus(a=1)>
shape_increasing_concave()
#> <shape: increasing concave, link = log>
shape_increasing(value = c(at = 0, value = 0))
#> <shape: increasing, link = log, f(0) = 0>
shape_convex(slope = c(at = 0.5, value = 0))
#> <shape: convex, link = log, f'(0.5) = 0>

# Settings by level, for a factor by with levels a and b.
shape_increasing(min_slope = c(a = 0, b = 0.2))
#> <shape: increasing, link = log, min_slope = (a = 0.0, b = 0.2)>
shape_increasing(value = list(at = 0, value = c(a = 0, b = 1)))
#> <shape: increasing, link = log, f(0) = (a = 0, b = 1)>
shape_convex(left_slope_by = "shared")
#> <shape: convex, link = log, one left slope for every level>

# A link onto the whole real line is rejected.
try(shape_concave(link = linkfunctions7::identity_link()))
#> Error : the link 'identity' maps onto (-Inf, Inf); a shape needs a link onto (0, Inf),
#>   such as log_link() or softplus_link().
